Travels to speak on the aforementioned receipts. So there is nothing on record to show that Sri Durga Travels stood 
closed by the time the enquiry was initiated as urged by the I Party. 


20. All these would indicate that the I Party has been well aware of the foul play made in the transaction and he 
could not improvise his case anymore. The principles of natural justice are not successfully shown to have been 
violated in initiating the disciplinary proceeding against the I Party. The factual matrix being so, the legal principles 
in the rulings in Abdulla A. Latif Shah vs. Bombay Port Trust and Others (992 () LLJ 226) and R K Gupta vs. 
Coal India LTD and others (993 (l) LLJ 93) relied upon by the I Party are not of any help to him. In the second 
ruling supra, the facts indicate that the purported charges are absolutely vague and so it is held that on vague 
allegation of charges the petitioner cannot be proceeded against. In the first ruling cited supra also so many laches 
from the side of the employer in the conduct of the Domestic Enquiry were detected, which, along with a finding that 
the charge sheet is delayed and stale led to the conclusion that such a charge sheet cannot be proceeded with since the 
enquiry held on it suffers from breach of natural justice. No such event intervenes in the case on hand disqualifying 
the charge sheet issued to the I Party preceding enquiry. On all these counts, I do not find any force in the argument 
raised by the I Party that the enquiry is vitiated by reason of its delayed initiation. 


2I. In the finding of the Enquiry Officer on culmination of the domestic enquiry, the charge levelled against the I 
Party / delinquent officer that his action of producing the false bills / documents for getting the LFC bills sanctioned 
was held as proved under Ex M-4 report dated 08.03.2004, marked Ex M4 in evidence before this Tribunal. The 
Enquiry Officer has arrived at the above finding after a full-fledged enquiry and by deeply analysing the extensive 
oral and documentary evidence adduced by the management through the Presenting Officer. Though the I Party has 
availed the opportunity to tender rebuttal evidence by examining him as a defence witness, later he preferred to 
withdraw from adducing defence evidence. His voluntary relinquishment of the right of adducing rebuttal evidence 
from his side would lead to the solitary conclusion that he has got nothing to put on record against what is proved 
against him by the II Party in the enquiry. The proved act committed by the I Party by producing false and 
manipulated documents is absolutely unbecoming of a bank official. The purpose of producing the forged and fake 
documents Ex M4 and M5/I before the bank is for getting the LFC bill sanctioned very immediately in respect of the 
rest of the amount he claimed. On facts as well as on law, the finding drawn by the Enquiry Officer is neither perverse 
nor biased, but simply based on the concrete materials and evidence brought on record by the II Party. Therefore, the 
finding rendered by the Enquiry Officer does not suffer from any infirmities nor does it stand vitiated by any 
illegalities. Hence , the contention raised by the I Party that the finding of the Enquiry Officer is perverse, biased and 
arbitrary assumes no force or acceptance. Ergo, the said finding does not warrant any interference from this Tribunal. 
With this view, issue no. | is answered against the I Party. 


22. Issue no. 2: An argument is advanced by the learned counsel for the II Party with reference to the ruling of 
the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation rep. by its Chief Law 
Officer, vs. BMTC and State Transport Naukarara Sangha (ILR 20ll Karnataka 2037) that the Central 
Reference cannot be maintainable as this Tribunal gets jurisdiction u/s |l(A) of the ID Act only on dismissal or 
discharge of workman. In the given case, the punishment imposed by the disciplinary authority on the I Party is 
reduction in scale of pay by two stages with cumulative effect. As a matter of fact and as per law, an order reducing 
employees’ pay scale can be challenged u/s (A) of the Act if the reduction is deemed as a disciplinary action. The 
commentary of Sec |l(A) assertively explain that the provision empowers labour courts , Tribunal and National 
Tribunals to “review and modify” disciplinary action including those resulting in pay reductions if they find the 
punishment to be disproportionate to the misconduct. Therefore, the I Party cannot be found fault with in approaching 
the Central Government seeking redressal of his grievance against the punishment imposed on him by the authority 
concerned by getting the matter referred to this Tribunal for adjudication. Therefore, this argument raised by the II 
Party cannot be accepted. 


23. On facts, on receipt of finding from the Enquiry Officer, the Disciplinary Authority proposed a punishment 
and issued notice to the I Party calling for his explanation. After getting his explanation and evaluating the entire 
factual matrix, the Disciplinary Authority as per its order (Ex M6) dated 23.06.2004 imposed the punishment of 
reduction in scale of pay by two stages with cumulative effect. The authority also passed an administrative order on 
the very same date i.e., 23.06.2004 directing the I Party to make good the amount of Rs. 9,000/-, the amount availed 
by him in advance under LFC with simple interest @ 0.75% p.a. immediately. 


24. Vehement argument is advanced on behalf of the I Party that by taking refund of Rs. [9000/- from him and 
by imposing reduction in scale of pay by 2 stages with cumulative effect, the II Party has imposed dual punishment on 
him which amounts to double jeopardy which is prohibited in law. As a matter of fact, refund of Rs. 9000/- availed 
by the I Party as LFC advance cannot be characterised as a punishment. Instead it is only a recovery of the money 
wrongly availed by him by producing unreliable and invalid documents as an advance towards LFC claim. By taking 
refund of it, the II Party has done only recouping of the money wrongly parted with to its credit. Actually, punishment 
imposed on him is the one by reducing scale of pay by 2 stages with cumulative effect and that punishment in no way 
is vitiated by any intervening events or circumstances. 


836 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : FEBRUARY 2], 2026/PHALGUNA 2, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


25. On a close analysis of the entire facts and circumstances of the case, the impugned punishment imposed by 
the Disciplinary Authority under Ex M-6 dated 23.06.2004 and confirmed by the appellate authority under Ex M-7 
order dated 03..2004 do not appear to be disproportionate, arbitrary or illegal. No harm is done to the job prospects 
of the I Party by the impugned punishment. A reduction in the pay scale though brings about a substantial loss to the I 
Party on the monetary side, such an administrative intervention stands duly warranted and justified in terms of the 
misconduct committed. Reasonableness and legality of the punishment imposed has to be adjudged not from the point 
of view of the monetary loss caused to the delinquent officer but on a wider sense of the act of illegality and 
immorality committed by him to the employer establishment. When viewed so, I am of the definite view that the 
punishment imposed is strictly commensurate with the gravity of the misconduct / misdeed committed by the 
employee I Party. Therefore, I conclude by answering this issue that the punishment imposed by the Disciplinary 
Authority under Ex M6 and confirmed by the Appellate Authority under Ex M7 is not disproportional, excessive, 
arbitrary or illegal. Accordingly, the relief sought by the I Party to set aside Ex M6 order awarding punishment of 
reduction of scale of pay by 2 stages with cumulative effect and to direct the II party management to restore the same 
retrospectively from the date of its imposition and to further direct the II Party to grant the workman all the monetary 
benefits along with arrears also do fail. Hence it is concluded that the case and claim put forth by the I Party is devoid 
of merit and bereft of bona fides and it is liable to be dismissed. With this view, this issue is also answered against the 
I Party.

By order No. K-0/l-7/2020-IR dated 8.0i.202] the present industrial dispute has been referred for 
adjudication to this Tribunal in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (d) of sub-section () and sub-section (2A) 
of Section l0 the Industrial Disputes Act, !947 ([4 of 947) by the Central Government, with following schedule: 


“Whether Shri Santosh Kumar Singh, Bss Filed Engineer can be treated as workman? If so, whether the 
alleged termination of his services by the management of Nokia Solutions and Networks India Pvt. Ltd./ 
Vodafone Idea Limited is legal & justified? If not, to what relief the concerned workman is entitled to and 
from which date?" 

Accordingly, an industrial dispute No. 09/202] has been registered on 28.0.202]. 

On 03.08.202] claimant filed claim statement supported by an affidavit. 


Facts stated in the claim petition are in brief that claimant was initially appointed with the respondent; however 
without following the provision of retrenchment as provided under section 25 (F), 25 (G) & 25 (H) of the Industrial 
Dispute Act !947 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) his services were dispensed on 05.02.2020. 

On behalf of the respondent no. 2 statement of defense filed on !2.03.2023 and respondent no. | filed its written 
statement on |.09.2023 in which preliminary objection also taken by the respondent. 

After filing of the written statement by respondent, in spite of opportunities given to workman, he neither filed 
rejoinder nor evidence in support of his case on affidavit 

Accordingly heard learned counsel for respondent and gone through the records. 

In view of the above said facts the claimant/workman has not field any rejoinder/evidence in support of his case on 


affidavit, in spite of several opportunities given to him and taking into consideration the law as laid by the Hon'ble 
High Court in the case of V. K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court (7) and others 7967 (29) FLR 94 as under: 


“It is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to prove 
illegality of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the Court must fail. 
Whenever a workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of service if is imperative 
for him to file written statement before the Industrial Court setting out grounds on which the order is 
challenged and he must also produce evidence to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file 
written statement or produce evidence, the dispute referred by the State Government cannot be answered in 
favour of the workman and he would not be entitled to any relief.” 

In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding Officer, 

Labour Court (II), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (776) FLR 7764 Hon’ble Allahabad High Court has held as under: 
“The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., 
V.K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. /964 (49) 
FLR 38 and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. 7996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led 
by or on behalf of the workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In 
such a situation it is not necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead 
evidence to establish an allegation made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would be, 
who would fail if no evidence is led.”’ 

And by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. P.A.C.C.S.C. 

Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co-operative Bank Ltd. 2070 (726) FLR 529; wherein it has been held as 

under: 
“The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the shoulders of the 
respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to lead evidence first which he failed. 
A perusal of the impugned award also does not show that any evidence either oral or documentary was led 
by the respondent. In the case of no evidence, the reference has to be dismissed.”

As the workman has not filed any rejoinder/affidavit (examination-in-chief) so it is a case of no evidence filed on 
behalf of workman in support of case set up by her, liable to be dismissed. 
For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and; and the workman is not entitled for any relief.

AWARD 


The Government of India, Ministry of Labour by its order No. L-4202/9/2009- (IR (DU) dated 22™ May 
2009 referred the following Industrial dispute under section l0(l)(d) of the ID. Act, 947, requiring this tribunal to 
decide the question. 


“Whether the action of the management of Export Inspection Agency, in terminating the services of their 
workman Shri A. A. Mallikarjuna Rao with effect from 57 July 2008, is legal and justified? If not, what 
relief is the workman entitled to?” 


2. After receipt of the reference, it was numbered as ID No.30 of 2009, and notices were issued to both the workman 
and management. 


3. In response to the notice, Petitioner /workman filed the claim statement with the allegation that petitioner 
joined with the Respondent on March, 2002 at Bheemavaram office of the Respondent, and continuously worked with 
the respondent till 47 July 2008. Further, it is alleged that Respondent has terminated his services with effect from 57 
July 2008, without assigning any reason, and without issuing any charge sheet, and without conducting any inquiry. 
Further, it is alleged that Respondent has terminated the services of the petitioner arbitrarily and illegally, in violation 
of the procedure laid down under section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act. Further, Petitioner alleged that he 
requested the respondent to reinstate into the service, but all the efforts made by the petitioner became a futile 
exercise. Therefore, petitioner was left with no other option but to raise a dispute before the Assistant Labour 
Commissioner, Central, Vijayawada, who, in turn, conducted joint conciliation meeting with the Respondent. The 
conciliation officer could not arrive at an amicable settlement due to the non-cooperative and adamant attitude of the 
Respondent. Therefore, the Assistant Labour Commissioner sent the report to the Government of India, and which has 
been referred to the tribunal for adjudication. 


4. Per contra, Respondent has filed counter, and therein, he has contended that the averment made in the 
claim petition by the petitioner are frivolous, unwarranted, and illegal, and against the law. Further, it is submitted 
that the claim statement is not maintainable as the Respondent is a Central Government department, statutory body 
under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, and as such, this tribunal has no jurisdiction to 
try this suit. Further, it is contended that the Respondent is a statutory body established under section 7 of the Export 
Quality Control and Inspection Act, 963, and therefore, it is not covered within the definition of "industry" under the 
Act. Further, Respondent contend that the services of A. Mallikarjuna Rao was utilized by S.O. Bheemavaram for few 
hours a day on need basis, - part-time, intermittently, and wages were paid accordingly for the days he worked, and no 
appointment letter was issued as the services were of a casual nature on an intermittent basis. Further, it is contended 
that there was no work for him, and his services were discontinued by the S.O. Bheemavaram on 5" July 2008, as he 
was no longer required. Hence, the question of termination or issuing of any charge sheet or conducting an inquiry 
does not arise. Further, it is contended that Petitioner was not a regular employee of the Department. The question of 
his claiming scale of pay, overtime, PF, etc., does not arise. He was utilized on need-based work only, and the 
question of eliminating him from services does not arise. Further, it is contended that petitioner was never appointed 
to any regular post in the Respondent, Export Inspection Agency, Chennai sub-office, Bhimavaram, and his services 
were utilized on a need basis as and when work of an occasional and intermittent nature was available. Further, it is 
contended that the services of the petitioner were utilized for a few hours a day on a need basis intermittently, and 
wages were paid accordingly for the days he worked. He was not assigned the duties of Group D employees at any 
point in time, as there was other permanent employees to look after the regular work that is assigned to Group D 
employees. No appointment letter was ever issued, as the services were on an intermittent basis. Further, it is 
contended that petitioner worked on need-based work, fully knowing he has been paid wages as applicable to need- 
based work, and there was no contract between the petitioner and the Respondent that he would be regularized or paid 
wages as is being paid to regularly appointed Group D employees. Therefore, petitioner may not equate his need- 
based work with that of regular employees. Further, it is contended that as per Export Inspection Agency statutory 
recruitment rules, 980, amended up to 3!° December 986, the post of Group D (peon) is filled with a candidate 
having an age between |8 to 25 years. Qualification: Middle school certificate and knowledge of reading 
English/Hindi. The candidates who meet the requirements are called for an employment exchange, or through 
newspaper advertisement. Such candidates are required to be considered by selection committee, which shall make 
recommendations to the appointing authority regarding appointment or otherwise. And petitioner has not come in that 
category. The petitioner neither applied for appointment nor was considered by the selection committee. Therefore, it 
is prayed that the petition is devoid of merit and liable to be dismissed with costs. 


In support of the averments made in the claim statement, the petitioner has examined witness WWI and also 
filed the documents, Exhibit ४ to W9. On the other hand, the Respondent has filed the documents in support of 
contention the copies of statement of payment of part-time casual labor engagement for the years 2005 to 2006, 
2007, and 2008. 


[भाग ]--खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 2, 2026/फाल्गुन 2, 947 849 


In view of the submissions made by either parties, the following issues arise for determination in the present 
case: - 


l. Whether the Respondent the direction ( I & A C) Export Inspection Council of India, is covered within the 
definition of “Industry” as provided under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947. 


2. Whether the action of management of Export Inspection Agency, in terminating the services of workman, Shri A. 
Mallikarjuna Rao, with effect from 5" July 2008, is legal and justified? 


3. To what relief, if any, is workman entitled to? 
Findings 
Issue No. I:- 


In this context, Respondent has submitted that the Respondent, Export Inspection Agency, Chennai, is a 
regulatory authority operating under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry in the field of pre-shipment inspection of 
notified commodities, and it was set up by the Central Government under Section 7 of the export, (quality control, and 
inspection Act, 963). Therefore, the claim statement is not maintainable as the Respondent is a Central Government 
department, statutory body under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. And as such, this 
Tribunal has no jurisdiction to try this dispute under the provision of Industrial Dispute Act, |947. 


In this context, Petitioner, in his chief statement affidavit, has nowhere stated that contention of Respondent 
in the counter, that the Export Inspection Agency of Chennai is a regulatory and operational body, and it does not 
come under the definition of "industry" as provided under the Industrial Disputes Act, is incorrect: undisputedly 
Respondent is governed by the Export, (quality control, inspection Act, 963). And its main function is to ensure 
quality control and pre-shipment inspection for goods being exported from India. Therefore, the Respondent Export 
Inspection Council of India, is not covered under the definition of "industry" as provided under Section 2F of the 
Industrial Disputes Act. The Export Inspection Counsel operate under the separate Act which focus on advising the 
Government and ensure quality control for Export rather than its activities like inspection and certification are part of 
its function as a statutory body for trade not industrial activity as defined under I.D Act !947. industrial Disputes 
Therefore, the claim statement of the petitioner raising industrial dispute is not maintainable under the provision of 
Industrial Dispute Act. This issue is decided against the petitioner. 


Issue No.II:- 


In this context, petitioner, in his claim statement, has alleged that he joined the service of the Respondent on 
March 2002, at the Bhimavaram office, and worked till 4" July 2008, and his service has been terminated by reports 
without assigning any reason in gross violation of the provision contained under Section 25F and 25N of the 
Industrial Disputes Act. Petitioner has alleged that has termination order dated 57 July 2008 is illegal, liable to be set 
aside. In support of his allegation. Petitioner has filed the affidavit of chief statement of his witness ४१७], Therein 
१४५४] has reiterated the averment made in the claim statement. Whereas, in the cross-examination, WW has stated 
that the Assistant director of Respondent management, Shri G. V. George, engaged him on duty and there was no 
notification published for the post in any newspaper. Further, WW] states that on the verbal request of the Assistant 
director, he joined the work. Further, witness states that there was no designation for his post and no appointment 
letter was issued to him. His name was not sponsored through the employment exchange. Further, the WW state that 
he felt there was vacancy for four posts, and he may be absorbed in one post and he doesn't know whether the four 
vacant posts were sanctioned or not. Further, WWI witness states that he has made four representations to the 
Chennai head office and also to the office bearer of the Respondent office in the year 200I, and he was paid Rs. 20/- 
per day and later on he was paid Rs. 25/-, and Rs. 35/-, and lastly, he was getting Rs. 70/- per day. Further, the 
witness states that it is not correct to say that the amount of Rs. 20/- was paid to him in the year 200! for hourly basis. 
The witness WWI admitted that it is not an industry, but it is a central government agency, and there was no 
manufacturing or production in the Respondent office. Thus, in view of the statement made by the witness WWI in 
his cross-examination, it manifests that the petitioner had worked as a daily wager in the Respondent office and he 
was not issued any appointment letter for the post. The document filed by the petitioner in support of his allegation do 
not support the averment of the petitioner that he was appointed in the Respondent office on Group D post. However, 
petitioner has not filed any appointment letter, Attendance Register or salary slip in support of his averment that he 
was appointed by the Respondent. The document exhibit W3, is a letter dated 267 December 2008, issued by the 
Export Inspection Agency Chennai in respect of the representation of petitioner, A. Mallikarjuna Rao, it is mentioned 
therein that the petitioner A. Mallikarjuna Rao had worked intermittently for a few hours a day on a daily basis, as 
and when his services were required. Further, it is mentioned that no order of appointment was issued to A. 
Mallikarjuna Rao at any point of time. 


As regard the contention of the petitioner that he has been terminated by the Respondent from the 
employment in gross violation of section 25F and 25N of the ID Act, Before examining the legality of termination of 
Petitioner it would be apposite to mention the relevant provision contained under section 25F of the IT Act, as 
extracted hereunder:- 


850 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : FEBRUARY 2], 2026/PHALGUNA 2, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


25-F. Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen:- No workman employed in any industry who has been 
in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until- 


(a) the workman has been given one month's notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment and the 
period of notice has expired, or the workman has been paid in lieu of such notice, wages for the period of the 
notice. 


[xxx] 


(b) the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation which shall be equivalent to fifteen days' 
average pay [for every completed year of continuous service] or any part thereof in excess of six months; and 


(c) notice in the prescribed manner is served on the appropriate Government [or such authority as may be specified by 
the appropriate Government by notification in the Official Gazette]. 


Further, in this context, Hon’ble Court has laid down principles in respect of continuous service under the 
provision contained under section 25F of the ID Act 947 and also burden of proof these decision of Hon’ble Court 
are being discussed as here under:- 


(a).Further, in Rajasthan State Ganganagar S. Mills Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan and Anr. (2004) Apex Court held: 


"It was the case of the workman that he had worked for more than 240 days in the year concerned. This 
claim was denied by the appellant. It was for the claimant to lead evidence to show that he had worked for 240 days in 
the year preceding the date of his termination. He has filed an affidavit. It is statement which is in his favor and that 
cannot be regarded as sufficient evidence for any Court or Tribunal to come to the conclusion that in fact the claimant 
had worked for 240 days in a year." 


(b).In the case of Mohan Lal v. Management, BEL 498] SCC P. 225. Hon'ble Apex Court held:-

Thus, the allegation of the petitioner that Respondent has been terminated him from services in violation of 
the provision contained under Section 25(f) of the ID Act is not established and proved from the evidence on record. 
Therefore, Petitioner is not entitled to for any compensation or notice pay or notice as per provision of section 25F of 
the Act. Thus, the action of the respondent management in terminating his services is not illegal. This issue is decided 
against the petitioner, the workman. 


Issue No. IV:- 


In view of the finding given in issue No. II, the petitioner failed to prove that he was terminated in violation of the 
provision contained under Section 25F of the ID Act. Therefore, Petitioner is not entitled to any relief, and the 
Petition is liable to be dismissed. 


AWARD 


The action of the Respondent in terminating the services of the petitioner, vide order dated 05.07.2008 is held legal 
and justified. Petition is devoid of merit hence stands dismissed. The Reference is answered. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.

The Government of India, Ministry of Labour by its order No. L- 400/06/20l4(IR(DU) dated 2™ June

l.“Whether the demand of workmen of BSNL, Eluru is legal and justified. If not, what other relief the 
workmen are entitled to?" 


2. After receipt of the reference, it was numbered as ID No.|0 of 20I4, and notices were issued to both the 
workmen and the management. 


3. On the service of notice Petitioner has filed claim statement whereas Respondent has filed counter. In the claim 
statement Petitioner union has alleged that the Respondent Management showing partisans attitude against the 
Petitioner Union and ill treatment to member of the Petitioner union and some other unrecognized union while N.F.T. 
E union is the recognized union. The member of the N.F.T.E union are shown undue favoritism in posting their 
members at comfortable places according to wishes of the recognize union whereas the Petitioner union members are 
facing ill treatment from the Respondent Management. Further, Petitioner has made reference of two instances for the 
alleged partisans attitude of Respondent Management. 


Firstly, Petitioner alleged that S. Durga Rao Telecom Mechanic Eluru got fracture his leg during the out 
door duties and he was given indoor duties on this ground at MDF station Telephone Bhavan Eluru, Surprisingly he 
has been transferred to perform outdoor duties vide order dated 3l-07-20l3 in order to accommodate M. 
Yesuratnam, who belonged to NFTE Union. Further, it is alleged that the transfer order of S. Durga Rao issued on 3[- 
07-20l3 which was the retirement date of the Respondent GM to show favors to M. Yesuratnam without assigning 
any reason. The Respondent Management consider similar cases sympathetically whereas in the case of Durga Rao, 
he was forced to take voluntary retirement, as he was unable to perform his outdoor duties. Further, other instance of 
the workman has been referred who has been accommodated belongs to recognize union. The second instance to 
show the partisans attitude of management with claim statement has been referred by the Petitioner that Smt A Mary 
Grace belongs to Petitioner union and she passed intermediate and was posted in the office of GM instead of utilizing 
her services in the administrative office and she has been transferred frequently and at present she is entrusted the 
duty of watchwoman further it is alleged that she is being harassed and forced to be on duty till 0 PM daily. Shri A. 
Mary Grace made several requests to the union and also made several requests to management by in vain. Whereas 
the woman workman belonging recognize union has been accommodated on the comfortable posting. 


Further it is submitted that women employee belonging to Group D services were promoted as GMs and 
TMs and are supposed to posted for outdoor duties. However, they are accommodated in the GM’s office working as 
‘Group D employees but drawing salaries as TMs. But in the case of Smt. A. Jayasree, Test Category Group D was 
transferred from GM office to MDF Telephone Bhavan to work on par with other TMs. As the Smt. A. Jayasree 
belongs to the Petitioner union she has been transferred to the GM office. Further Petitioner alleges that the union 
raise the disputes before the Asst. Labour Commissioner for redressal of the grievances of the employees in general 
such as issues periodicals like Soaps, towels chappals etc., to the members of the staff though they are entitled to 
similarly night allowances implementation of the tenure transfer repairs to pump sets water facilities at telephone 
building and all above the welfare facilities are required to be provided by Respondent management and when the 
same are not provided the Petitioner Union take up the issue for discussion before the ALC Vijayawada /RLC 
Hyderabad to maintain the efficient working of the employees. The union therefore prayed that Respondent be 
directed to provide TA and DA to the president secretary of the Petitioner Union and also direct the Respondent 
management to teach all the employees on an equal footing, irrespective of their affiliation with union, in the matter 
of transfers. 


4. Per contra Respondent has filed counter, and therein, it is contended that all material allegations made in 
the claim statement except that are admitted hereunder are denied. Further, it is contended that the respondent denies 
the allegation made by the petitioner that the Respondent management is showing partisan attitude against the 
members of the petitioner union and showing favoritism to the members of recognized union. The action of transfers, 
and allotment of work, and giving allowances etc. are as per the rules in force. Further, Respondent contended that 
management has shown the partition attitude against the transfer of S. Durgha Rao. Further, it is contended that after 
the fracture in the leg of Durga Rao, he was given the indoor duty at MDF Eluru. Respondent contended that there 
was acute shortage in TM cadre in outdoor plant at Eluru, and due to a shortage of outdoor TMs, there was a setback 
in rending services to the customer. The petitioner, S Durga Rao TM Eluru, has requested a one-year exemption from 
outdoor duties hence, he was posted to indoor duties. He served in indoor duty for more than 24 years before the issue 
of the local transfer to an outdoor unit. His stay in indoor duties is more than stay of others at the telephone exchange, 
Eluru. The official retired voluntarily on I“ February 204.

Further, Respondent contended that he specifically denies the allegation made by the petitioner that 
Smt. T. Jayasree Grade D, is being transferred frequently, and entrusted watch woman duties, and was harassed to do 
duty till 0 PM daily for the reason that she belongs to member of the petitioner union. The respondent submits that 
Smt. T. Jayasree Grade D was initially posted in the office of G M T D, Eluru. Subsequently she was posted to H DE 
Urban Eluru for watch woman duties. Later on request of T. Jayasree Grade D, she was transferred from watch 
woman duties to indoor duties at Main Telephone Exchange. Therefore, the action of respondent is in accordance 
with the rules in force, mainly considering the request of the said employee. Each of the material allegation made by 
the petitioner is specifically denied. Further Respondent contended that, there is no rule prescribed for settlement of 
the payment of T A/D A to the representative of the union on par with the management representative for attending 
the conciliation meeting at Assistant Commissioner of Labour, and hence the said demand was not considered. 
Further Respondent contended that the demand of supply of tool bag, periodical arrangement, are being given as per 
the schedule and being continued subject to availability of the funds. At present there is no round the clock duties for 
the cadre of T.M.S. and T.T.A.X., hence the night duty allowances are not being paid. Further, respondent contended, 
repair of the pump set are being taken up immediately and temporary arrangement during repairs are also made for 
provision of the water facility at Telephone Buildings. The Respondent specifically denies the allegation made by the 
petitioner that the Respondent management is supporting the recognize union and working against the interest of the 
workmen. This Respondent submits that management acts as per the rules and policies and guidelines from the circle 
of and do not show any partisan attitude and favoritism to any member of union as contended by the petitioner. 
Further it is contended that there is no ruling for payment of T A/D A to representative of the union on par with the 
management representative for attending the conciliation meeting. Assistant Labour Commissioner, hence, the 
demand was not considered by the respondents. 


Respondent prayed to dismiss the petition. petitioner in oral evidence chief statement affidavit of K.S.R. 
Murthy, as WW and has also filed documents as per list from | to 8. Petitioner has also filed written argument. 


on the basis of the pleadings of either parties, following issues emerge for determination in the 
present case: - 


l. whether the demand of workman BSNL, Eluru is legal and justified? 
2. To what relief, if any, the workman are entitled to? 

Finding 

Issue No. I :- 


In this context, petitioner has filed chief statement affidavit of the witness WWI and witness in his affidavit has 
reiterated the allegations made in the petition. This witness has also exhibited the documents. This witness, para 7 of 
affidavit has stated that he rely on the documents filed on 6"" December 20]6, by the petitioner, and the same may 
be marked as Exhibits WWI to WW9. But this witness has not stated in his affidavit that what facts he is going to 
establish by these documents. Thus, the contents of the document are not roved by evidence of ४४५४]. Moreover, 
this witness, despites sufficient opportunity, did not turn up for cross-examination. Therefore, the evidence of the 
petitioner was closed by the court after affording the sufficient number of opportunities. In the absence of cross- 
examination of witness WWI, the evidence of this witness cannot be read in evidence as per the principle of 
evidence. Therefore, Petitioner failed to substantiate his allegation by any, oral or documentary evidence. 


However, as regard the allegation of the petitioner that Sri S. Durga Rao, T.A. Eluru, and Smt. A. Mary 
Grace have been transferred due to partisan attitude of Respondent management, Petitioner has failed to substantiate 
his allegation by any cogent and reliable relevant evidence that the action of the Respondent management in 
transferring these workmen was mala fide or in contravention of the certified standing orders or employment 
contract, or either it resulted in a change of service condition. However, as regard the demand of TA/DA, that has 
been declined by the respondent management, as shown in the minutes of the conciliation proceeding held on 50 
February 2024. The demand has been discussed and declined before the Assistant Labor Commissioner 0, 
Therefore, Petitioner has utterly failed to prove the allegation of claim statement by any relevant evidence. Thus, the 
demand raised by the workmen petitioners of BSNL, Eluru, is not legal and justified. Issue is decided against the 
petition Workman. 


Issue No. II:- 


In view of the findings given at Issue No. I, the demands of the workmen of BSNL, Eluru, are not justified 
and legal. Therefore, petitioner workmen are not entitled to any relief. The petition, sans merit, and is liable to be 
dismissed. 


AWARD 


The demand of the workmen of petitioner BSNL, Eluru, is held not legal and justified. The petition claim 
statement of the Petitioner, sans merit, hence dismissed reference is answered accordingly. Award is passed 
accordingly.

Order 


In view of the above said facts the Management and Applicant has not appear before the Tribunal and Management 
not filed any written statement/ evidence in support of his case affidavit, in spite of several opportunities given to him 
and taking into consideration the law as laid by the Hon'ble High Court in the case of V. K. Raj Industries v. Labour 
Court (7) and others 7967 (29) FLR 94 as under: 


“It is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to prove illegality 
of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the Court must fail. Whenever a 
workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of service if is imperative for him to file 
written statement before the Industrial Court setting out grounds on which the order is challenged and he must 
also produce evidence to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file written statement or produce 
evidence, the dispute referred by the State Government cannot be answered in favour of the workman and he 
would not be entitled to any relief.” 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding Officer, 
Labour Court (II), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (7768) FLR 7764 Hon’ble Allahabad High Court has held as under: 


“The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., V.K. 
Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. /984 (49) FLR 38 
and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. 7/996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led by or on 
behalf of the workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In such a 
situation it is not necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead evidence to 
establish an allegation made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would be, who would fail 
if no evidence is led.” 


And by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. P.A.C.C.S.C. 
Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co-operative Bank Ltd. 2070 (726) FLR 59; 


Since 2022 workman is not present in-spite of notice and no written statement has been filed by the management in 
support of his case, the claims liable to be dismissed. 


For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and the workman is not entitled for any relief. 
Justice ARVIND KUMAR MISHRA, Presiding Officer

कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रुप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने
